references.text: Jabin, king of Hazor, is mentioned as the leader who gathered the kings against Israel, explaining why Joshua returned to conquer Hazor
The continuation of the conquest of Hazor, where the city was burned with fire
A similar pattern where Joshua completely destroyed a city and struck its king with the sword, just as he did with Jericho
Joshua conquered Makkedah and struck the king with the sword, the same pattern as with the king of Hazor
Hazor is mentioned again during Deborah's time as the headquarters of King Jabin, confirming the city's historical significance as 'head over all these kingdoms'
Hazor is listed among the cities that Solomon rebuilt, showing the city's continued strategic importance
Hazor was conquered by the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser, illustrating the city's fate in later times
